/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence

The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.

Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `instHasPicScheme`. -/
instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩

/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**

Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection

```
(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
```

for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers
(tangent-space computation at the identity, `Pic⁰` degree theory) can compose
with its `homEquiv` to transfer line-bundle data to scheme points. -/

locally of finite type, a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
`k`-subschemes), combined with Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 (under the `k`-rational
point of `[HasRationalPoint C]`, the plain relative functor `picSharp C`
coincides with the étale-sheafified one, so the same scheme represents it).
All three conjuncts of the existential — representability, local finiteness,
separatedness — are parts of that one Kleiman theorem.

The conditionality on `[HasRationalPoint C]` is essential for truth: without
a section, `Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` need not even be a Zariski sheaf. -/
noncomputable instance instHasPicScheme {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasRationalPoint C] : HasPicScheme C :=
  ⟨sorry⟩

namespace PicScheme

/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence

The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.

Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `instHasPicScheme`. -/
instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩

/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**

Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection

```
(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
```

for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers

1	\chapter{The Jacobian as an abelian variety}
2	\label{chap:Jacobian}
3	
4	Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field
5	\(k\), with genus \(g(C)\).  The Jacobian is constructed uniformly as the
6	identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the Picard scheme.  It is an abelian
7	variety of dimension \(g(C)\); when \(g(C)=0\), it is \(\Spec k\).
8	
9	\section{Albanese objects}
10	
11	\begin{definition}[Albanese universal property of a pointed curve]\leanok
12	  \label{def:IsAlbanese}
13	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlbanese}
14	  Let \(P \in C(k)\).  An abelian variety \(J\) together with a pointed
15	  morphism \(\iota_P \colon C \to J\) is an \emph{Albanese object} for
16	  \((C,P)\) if every pointed morphism \(f \colon C \to A\) to an abelian
17	  variety factors uniquely through \(\iota_P\): there is a unique morphism of
18	  \(k\)-schemes \(g \colon J \to A\) such that
19	  \[
20	    P \circ \iota_P = \eta_J,
21	    \qquad
22	    f = \iota_P \circ g.
23	  \]
24	\end{definition}
25	
26	\begin{remark}
27	  \label{rem:IsAlbanese_typeclasses}
28	  The phrase ``abelian variety'' includes the group structure, properness,
29	  smoothness, and geometric irreducibility of both \(J\) and every target
30	  \(A\).  These are hypotheses of the universal property, rather than extra
31	  conclusions inside it.
32	\end{remark}
33	
34	\subsection{The universal morphism}
35	
36	\begin{definition}[The Albanese universal morphism]\leanok
37	  \label{def:IsAlbanese_ofCurve}
38	  \uses{def:IsAlbanese}
39	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlbanese.ofCurve}
40	  An Albanese structure on \((C,P,J)\) determines a distinguished morphism
41	  \(\iota_P \colon C \to J\), called its universal morphism.
42	\end{definition}
43	
44	\begin{lemma}[Pointed condition]\leanok
45	  \label{lem:IsAlbanese_comp_ofCurve}
46	  \uses{def:IsAlbanese, def:IsAlbanese_ofCurve}
47	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlbanese.comp_ofCurve}
48	  The universal morphism satisfies \(P \circ \iota_P = \eta_J\).
49	\end{lemma}
50	
51	\begin{lemma}[Universal factorisation]\leanok
52	  \label{lem:IsAlbanese_exists_unique_ofCurve_comp}
53	  \uses{def:IsAlbanese, def:IsAlbanese_ofCurve}
54	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlbanese.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp}
55	  Every pointed morphism \(f \colon C \to A\) to an abelian variety factors
56	  uniquely as \(f=\iota_P\circ g\) through a morphism of \(k\)-schemes
57	  \(g \colon J \to A\).
58	\end{lemma}
59	
60	\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of the Albanese object]\leanok
61	  \label{thm:IsAlbanese_unique}
62	  \uses{def:IsAlbanese, def:IsAlbanese_ofCurve}
63	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.IsAlbanese.unique}
64	  If \((J_1,\iota_1)\) and \((J_2,\iota_2)\) are Albanese objects for
65	  \((C,P)\), there is a unique morphism \(e \colon J_1\to J_2\) satisfying
66	  \(\iota_2=\iota_1\circ e\).
67	\end{theorem}
68	
69	\begin{proof}\leanok
70	  The universal property of \(J_1\) applied to \(\iota_2\) gives
71	  \(e \colon J_1\to J_2\); that of \(J_2\) applied to \(\iota_1\) gives
72	  \(e' \colon J_2\to J_1\).  Both \(e\circ e'\) and the identity of \(J_1\)
73	  factor \(\iota_1\) through itself, so uniqueness gives
74	  \(e\circ e'=\mathrm{id}_{J_1}\); similarly
75	  \(e'\circ e=\mathrm{id}_{J_2}\).  The original universal property gives the
76	  required uniqueness of \(e\).
77	\end{proof}
78	
79	\begin{remark}
80	  \label{rem:IsAlbanese_unique_iso}
81	  Consequently the Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism
82	  compatible with the universal morphism.
83	\end{remark}
84	
85	\section{A uniform Jacobian witness}
86	
87	\begin{definition}[Jacobian witness]\leanok
88	  \label{def:JacobianWitness}
89	  \uses{def:IsAlbanese, def:genus}
90	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.JacobianWitness}
91	  A \emph{Jacobian witness} for \(C\) consists of a single \(k\)-scheme \(J\),
92	  an abelian-variety structure on \(J\), a proof that \(J\) is smooth of
93	  relative dimension \(g(C)\), and, for every \(P\in C(k)\), an Albanese
94	  structure on \((C,P,J)\).
95	\end{definition}
96	
97	\begin{remark}
98	  \label{rem:JacobianWitness_quantifier_order}
99	  The same \(J\) works for every marked point.  Replacing \(P\) by another
100	  rational point translates the universal morphism by an automorphism of
101	  \(J\), so it does not change the underlying abelian variety.
102	\end{remark}
103	
104	\begin{remark}
105	  \label{rem:JacobianWitness_smooth_redundancy}
106	  Smoothness is implied by smoothness of relative dimension \(g(C)\).  It is
107	  nevertheless useful to record both the abelian-variety property and the
108	  dimension assertion as parts of the witness.
109	\end{remark}
110	
111	\subsection{The Picard witness \(J=\Pic^0_{C/k}\)}
112	\label{sec:picardJacobianWitness}
113	
114	\begin{theorem}[A Jacobian witness for a pointed curve]
115	  \label{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint}
116	  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:genus, thm:fga_pic_representability,
117	    thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus,
118	    thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar, def:has_rational_point}
119	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint}
120	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over \(k\)
121	  possessing a \(k\)-rational point. Then the identity component
122	  \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for \(C\).
123	\end{theorem}
124	
125	\begin{proof}
126	  \uses{lem:curve_geometrically_integral, def:inst_has_pic_scheme,
127	    lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus, lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}
128	  Representability of the relative Picard functor
129	  (\cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme}, whose hypothesis is the rational point) gives
130	  \(\Pic_{C/k}\), and its identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is a group scheme,
131	  smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible by
132	  \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety}. Those four data are the first four fields of
133	  the witness; of the four, \cref{thm:pic0_smooth} and \cref{thm:pic0_proper} are
134	  the ones whose own proofs are still open.
135	
136	  Three further steps are needed, and each is isolated as a lemma because it does
137	  not follow from the four above.
138	
139	  First, the hypotheses must be reconciled: \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is constructed for a
140	  geometrically \emph{integral} curve, whereas a witness is required for a
141	  geometrically irreducible one. Geometric integrality is automatic
142	  (\cref{lem:curve_geometrically_integral}).
143	
144	  Second, the smoothness supplied by \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety} carries no
145	  relative dimension, while the witness records smoothness at the specific
146	  relative dimension \(g(C)\); the tangent-space identification
147	  \(T_0\Pic^0_{C/k}\cong H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\) of
148	  \cref{thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus} supplies the dimension, and
149	  \cref{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus} is the resulting refinement.
150	
151	  Third, the Albanese structure is required for \emph{every} \(P\in C(k)\) and for
152	  every genus, whereas \cref{thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar} is proved
153	  over an algebraically closed base field and for \(g(C) > 0\); the extension is
154	  \cref{lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}. Together these seven data form the
155	  required witness.
156	\end{proof}
157	
158	\begin{remark}[What the pointed witness settles and what it leaves open]
159	  \label{rem:pointed_witness_scope}
160	  \uses{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint, lem:curve_hypothesis_gap,
161	    def:inst_has_pic_scheme}
162	  \Cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint} separates the construction of
163	  the witness from the question of where the rational point comes from, and the two
164	  witnesses below are the two answers to that question:
165	  \cref{def:picardJacobianWitness} takes the point from
166	  \cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap} and \cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed}
167	  from \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}. Nothing beyond the choice of
168	  source distinguishes them.
169	
170	  This bears on the open question of \cref{rem:rational_point_scope}
171	  asymmetrically, and the asymmetry is worth recording. A theorem for a curve
172	  \emph{with} a rational point is exactly the statement above, so that formulation
173	  requires no mathematics beyond the obligations already listed there. The étale
174	  formulation is not obtained from it: representing
175	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) replaces \cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme} rather than
176	  supplying its hypothesis, so it needs a representability theorem for a different
177	  functor. That one formulation is nearer to hand is not an argument that it is the
178	  right claim to make.
179	\end{remark}

181	\begin{theorem}[The Picard identity component is a Jacobian witness]
182	  \label{def:picardJacobianWitness}
183	  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:genus, thm:fga_pic_representability,
184	    thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus,
185	    thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar}
186	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.picardJacobianWitness}
187	  The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for
188	  \(C\).
189	\end{theorem}
190	
191	\begin{proof}
192	  \uses{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint, lem:curve_hypothesis_gap,
193	    rem:pointed_witness_scope}
194	  Apply \cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint}, whose rational-point
195	  hypothesis is supplied by \cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap}. That hypothesis is the
196	  single genuine gap, and it is a gap only over a general base field: over an
197	  algebraically closed field it is \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed} and the
198	  witness is \cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed}.
199	\end{proof}

201	\begin{lemma}[A smooth geometrically irreducible curve is geometrically integral]
202	  \label{lem:curve_geometrically_integral}
203	  \leanok
204	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIntegral_of_curve}
205	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field \(k\).
206	  Then \(C\) is geometrically integral over \(k\).
207	\end{lemma}
208	
209	\begin{proof}
210	  \leanok
211	  \uses{lem:smooth_geometrically_reduced}
212	  A smooth morphism is geometrically reduced
213	  (\cref{lem:smooth_geometrically_reduced}), and a morphism that is both
214	  geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible is geometrically integral:
215	  for every field extension \(K/k\) the base change \(C_K\) is then both reduced
216	  and irreducible, hence integral.
217	\end{proof}
218	
219	\begin{lemma}[A smooth morphism is geometrically reduced]
220	  \label{lem:smooth_geometrically_reduced}
221	  \leanok
222	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced}
223	  A morphism of schemes \(f\colon X\to Y\) that is smooth of some relative
224	  dimension is geometrically reduced: for every field \(K\) and every morphism
225	  \(\Spec K\to Y\), the base change \(X\times_Y\Spec K\) is a reduced scheme.
226	\end{lemma}
227	
228	\begin{proof}
229	  \leanok
230	  \uses{lem:standard_smooth_over_domain_reduced}
231	  Smoothness is stable under base change, so it suffices to show that a scheme
232	  \(X\) smooth over a field \(K\) is reduced. Reducedness is local, and \(X\) is
233	  covered by affine opens \(\Spec S\) with \(S\) standard smooth over \(K\); each
234	  is reduced by \cref{lem:standard_smooth_over_domain_reduced} applied to the
235	  domain \(K\).
236	\end{proof}
237	
238	\begin{lemma}[A standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced]
239	  \label{lem:standard_smooth_over_domain_reduced}
240	  \leanok
241	  \lean{Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain}
242	  Let \(B\) be a domain and \(S\) a standard smooth \(B\)-algebra. Then \(S\) is
243	  reduced.
244	\end{lemma}
245	
246	\begin{proof}
247	  \leanok
248	  By the structure theorem for standard smooth algebras, \(S\) is étale over a
249	  polynomial ring \(P=B[x_1,\dots,x_n]\), which is again a domain. So it suffices
250	  to prove that a flat, formally unramified \(P\)-algebra \(S\) essentially of
251	  finite type over a domain \(P\) is reduced, étale algebras being flat, formally
252	  unramified and essentially of finite type.
253	
254	  Let \(F=\operatorname{Frac}(P)\). The algebra \(F\otimes_P S\) is formally
255	  unramified and essentially of finite type over the field \(F\), hence reduced.
256	  Since \(S\) is flat over \(P\) and \(P\to F\) is injective, the induced map
257	  \(S\cong P\otimes_P S\to F\otimes_P S\) is injective, so \(S\) embeds into a
258	  reduced ring and is therefore reduced.
259	\end{proof}

261	\begin{lemma}[The curve has a \(k\)-rational point]
262	  \label{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap}
263	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.hasRationalPoint_of_curve}
264	  \uses{def:has_rational_point}
265	  A smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve \(C\) over a field \(k\) has a
266	  \(k\)-rational point.
267	\end{lemma}
268	
269	\begin{proof}
270	  This assertion is \emph{false} as stated. A smooth proper geometrically
271	  integral curve need not have a \(k\)-rational point: a conic over \(\mathbb{Q}\)
272	  with no rational point is a genus-\(0\) example, and there are genus-\(2\)
273	  curves over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point. Over an algebraically closed
274	  field a rational point always exists, since a curve there is a nonempty
275	  Jacobson space whose closed points are rational.
276	
277	  The lemma is therefore stated here only to name the gap between the hypotheses
278	  of the witness and those of the Picard construction, and it is not provable in
279	  this form. Closing it requires either weakening the claim --- carry
280	  \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a hypothesis of the Jacobian itself, which proves
281	  something weaker than intended --- or replacing the input by a representability
282	  statement that needs no section, namely representability of the \'etale
283	  sheafification (\cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}). That choice is open. The algebraically
284	  closed case is not affected by it and is \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}.
285	\end{proof}

287	\begin{lemma}[A curve over an algebraically closed field has a rational point]
288	  \label{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}
289	  \leanok
290	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed}
291	  \uses{def:has_rational_point}
292	  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically
293	  closed field \(\bar k\). Then \(C\) has a \(\bar k\)-rational point.
294	\end{lemma}
295	
296	\begin{proof}
297	  \leanok
298	  Geometric irreducibility over the one-point base \(\Spec \bar k\) makes the
299	  underlying space of \(C\) irreducible, in particular nonempty, and smoothness makes
300	  \(C \to \Spec \bar k\) locally of finite type, so that space is a Jacobson space.
301	  A nonempty Jacobson space has a closed point \(x\). Over an algebraically closed
302	  field the residue field at a closed point of a scheme locally of finite type is
303	  \(\bar k\) itself, so \(x\) is the image of a section of \(C \to \Spec \bar k\),
304	  which is the required rational point.
305	\end{proof}

307	\begin{remark}[Which leaf is false and which is merely unproved]
308	  \label{rem:rational_point_scope}
309	  \uses{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap, lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed,
310	    def:inst_has_pic_scheme}
311	  \Cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap} and \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed} state the
312	  same conclusion under different hypotheses, and the pair delimits what is open. Over an
313	  arbitrary base field the statement is false, so it admits no proof and the witness built
314	  on it rests on an inconsistent hypothesis --- its consequences are vacuously true. Over
315	  an algebraically closed field the same statement is a theorem. So the open question is
316	  not the existence of a rational point in general, but which of two formulations is
317	  claimed over an arbitrary \(k\): representability of \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with
318	  \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a hypothesis, or representability of the \'etale
319	  sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which needs no section
320	  (\cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}). The remaining obligations of the witness ---
321	  representability itself (\cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme}), \cref{thm:pic0_smooth},
322	  \cref{thm:pic0_proper}, \cref{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus} and
323	  \cref{lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points} --- are of the other kind: true statements awaiting

326	  Discharging the rational point does not reduce their number. The identity component is
327	  defined only once \(\Pic_{C/k}\) exists, so over an algebraically closed field the
328	  discharge makes representability an obligation that must be met rather than one carried
329	  along inside the rational-point hypothesis. What changes is the kind of every remaining
330	  obligation, not the count.
331	\end{remark}

334	  \label{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed}

336	  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:picardJacobianWitness,

339	  \(\Pic^0_{C/\bar k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for every smooth proper
340	  geometrically irreducible curve \(C\), with no rational-point hypothesis.

358	  \label{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus}

360	  \uses{def:genus, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus, thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety}

371	  \cref{thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus}. Its \(k\)-dimension is \(g(C)\) by

376	  \label{lem:pic0_tangent_dimension_genus}

748:   \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Def.~4.1.}
749:   Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over a field
750:   \(k\), with a \(k\)-rational point. The \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\)
751:   is the \(k\)-scheme representing the relative Picard functor
752:   \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) (equivalently, by Kleiman \S 2 Thm.~2.5 under the
753:   rational point, its \'etale sheafification), supplied by
754:   \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}, equipped with the abelian-group-scheme
755:   structure of \cref{thm:pic_is_group_scheme}. The scheme is separated,
756:   locally of finite type over \(k\), and a disjoint union of open
757:   quasi-projective \(k\)-subschemes.
758: \end{definition}

761: \label{sec:fga_pic_lean_encoding}

763: The constructions above fit together through the following interfaces. The
